Good Memphis website design gets one thing right that many sites get wrong: the hours. A lot of the people who need a diner, a tire shop, a gym, a child care provider or a tow truck are not looking at nine in the morning. They are looking at eleven at night or five in the morning, on a phone, after work or before it. If your site does not say clearly that you are open, and how to reach you right now, the search moves on to someone else.

Dominion Web Design Pro writes sites that answer that customer. Maurice Johnson builds every page by hand from Big Sandy in East Texas, shows you a free demo before you spend anything, and charges one printed price.

Memphis website design for owners whose busy hours are after dark

Memphis has a real reason to be awake at night. FedEx runs its World Hub at Memphis International Airport, and in 2019 the company said the hub had about 11,000 team members and was the largest sort facility in the whole FedEx Express network. The main package sort happens overnight, with planes landing in a tight window after dark so packages can move on before morning. In October 2024 FedEx opened a new automated sort building at the hub, 1.3 million square feet over four levels, able to sort 56,000 packages an hour. Warehouses and trucking yards around the airport keep their own late schedules.

Think about who searches late. Someone coming off a shift wants a hot plate of food or a workout before bed. A parent working nights needs a sitter or a care center with early drop-off. A driver with a flat on the interstate needs a tire or a tow. None of them will dig through a menu called "Info" to find whether you are open.

Your site should put three things above the fold for that person: what you do, whether you are open right now, and a phone number that dials with one tap. Everything else, the story of the business, the photo gallery, the specials, can wait below.

The hours line is the most important sentence on the page

Owners are careful with logos and photos and careless with hours. Then hours change for a holiday or a staffing gap, the website still shows the old times, and a customer drives over to a locked door. Here is what a late-hours business site should do:

  • Show hours as real text, not inside an image, so phones and search engines can read them.
  • Spell out late nights: "open until 2 a.m. Friday and Saturday" beats a small grid nobody reads.
  • Say what happens after hours: voicemail, a callback by morning, an emergency number or an AI agent that answers.
  • Match your Google Business Profile exactly, including holiday changes.
  • Put a short banner on the home page when something changes, and take it down when it is over.

Google says local results depend mainly on relevance, distance and prominence, and its advice for doing well starts with complete, accurate business information. Hours are part of that. We will not promise a ranking, because nobody honest can. We will make sure your site and your profile tell the same story.

Visitors in town for Beale Street, the blues and the barbecue

On December 15, 1977, an act of Congress declared Beale Street the official Home of the Blues, and the street still pulls visitors downtown for live music, then on to a plate of ribs somewhere across town. Those guests arrive with a phone, a hotel address and a few hours to spend.

The numbers back it up. In Tennessee's 2024 county tourism figures, as reported by local news, Shelby County, home of Memphis, ranked second in the state, behind only Davidson County (Nashville) and ahead of Sevier County and the Smokies resort towns. Statewide, Tennessee counted 147 million visitors and $31.66 billion in direct visitor spending that year.

A visitor does not know your street, your parking or whether you take reservations. A restaurant, tour, shop or music venue that serves them needs a page that answers those questions in the first screen, a menu or price list as text rather than a blurry photo, and a map. Write it so someone who has never been to Memphis can find the door.

Restaurants and barbecue joints

Menu as text, hours by day, whether to call ahead, and what to expect on a busy weekend.

Tours and music venues

Times, what is included, how to book or buy, and where to park or get dropped off.

Shops downtown

What you sell, the cross streets, and hours that hold true on game and festival nights.

Every part of the metro has its own name

Memphis customers think in neighborhoods and suburbs, and they often search with those names. A page for each area you really serve beats a single line that says "Greater Memphis."

  • In the cityDowntown, Midtown, Cooper-Young, Overton Square, Orange Mound and Whitehaven. If your shop is in one of them, name it in the page title and the first paragraph, with cross streets and parking.
  • SuburbsGermantown, Bartlett and Collierville. A trade or service that drives out to customers here deserves a page for each, written about that town.
  • Across the state lineSouthaven, in Mississippi. If you work there, say so plainly, since a customer there may assume a Memphis business will not come.

A Black-owned builder, if that matters to you

Memphis is a majority-Black city: Census Bureau estimates put the Black share of residents at about 63 percent, against roughly 16 percent for Tennessee as a whole.

Dominion Web Design Pro is a Black-owned business; Maurice Johnson owns it and builds the sites. Some Memphis owners want to know that, and some do not care. Either way, you get the same thing: the person who writes your pages is the person you talk to. You can read more on our Black-owned web design page. We do not claim any minority business certification.

Prices, help nearby and how we work

Starter is $497 for five hand-written pages, live in 7 to 14 days. Pro is $997 for a ten-page site with a photo gallery, local SEO setup including your Google Business Profile, your Google reviews on the site and ten city pages. Agency is $1,997 for keyword research across your area and a page for each town and service worth having, delivered in waves with the first live inside two weeks. All three prices are one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are included while you keep the AI agent, or $49 a month without it. We do not sell page counts.

A website is one piece. For the rest of the business, Memphis has free help worth a phone call:

  • Tennessee SBDC, Memphis officeHosted by Southwest Tennessee Community College, with its main office at the Maxine A. Smith Center on East Shelby Drive and a satellite desk at the Greater Memphis Chamber downtown. Consulting is free.
  • Greater Memphis ChamberIts Small Business Council offers advocacy, programs and networking for smaller firms, and its small business pages point owners to SCORE mentors and to Epicenter and Start Co. for startups.
  • EpicenterA Memphis organization that runs accelerators and a nine-week CO.STARTERS course for people launching a product or service, and that works with the City of Memphis on the 800 Initiative to grow Black-owned firms.
  • City of Memphis Office of Business Diversity and ComplianceUnder the city's Equal Business Opportunity ordinance it is the certification office for minority- and women-owned firms that want work on city-funded projects. If you bid on city jobs, your site should list any certification you hold.

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in Memphis. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

Common questions

How much does Memphis website design cost for a small business?

Prices run from do-it-yourself builder plans to agency projects that cost thousands, and many builders only name a figure after a sales call. Dominion Web Design Pro prints its prices: Starter is $497 for five pages, Pro is $997 for ten pages plus ten city pages and local SEO setup, and Agency is $1,997 for a page for each town and service worth having, all one time. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep the AI agent.

My shop is open late. How should my website show that?

Write the hours as plain text on every page, near the top, with the days spelled out, and make sure they match your Google Business Profile exactly. If some services stop earlier than the doors close, say so. If you are open around the clock, say what that means: is the counter staffed, or is it a phone line? Customers who drive over at 3 a.m. and find a dark lot do not come back.

Is this page about Memphis, Tennessee, or the Memphis design style?

Memphis, Tennessee. Some people searching for Memphis web design are looking for a bold, retro graphic style that shares the name. This page is about building websites for businesses in and around the city of Memphis.

Can you write pages for Germantown, Collierville or Southaven too?

Yes, for any town you really serve, on either side of the state line. The Pro package includes ten city pages, each researched and written for one place, and Agency starts with keyword research across your area to decide which towns earn a page. A page about Southaven should say something true about working in Southaven, not repeat the Memphis page with a new name.

Can the phone get answered when I am closed?

That is what the AI phone agent is for. The Agency package includes setting one up; the agent is free for 7 days, then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time, and it is not part of the one-time price. Pro includes an AI chat widget that answers visitors on the site and takes a name and number, free for 14 days and then $297 a month.

See your website before you pay for it

Give us your business name and what you do, and a demo site gets built for you to look at on your own phone. If you like it, pick a package. If you do not, you have spent nothing but the minute it took to look.
